newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-PRASAD RIPS THROUGH S.AFRICAN BATTING.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PRASAD RIPS THROUGH S.AFRICAN BATTING.

text.p: Fast bowler Venkatesh Prasad struck four times before lunch, lifting India's hopes of restricting South Africa's score to less than 500 on the second day of their second cricket test at Eden Gardens on Thursday.
Resuming from an overnight score of 339 for two wickets, South Africa were 402 for seven at lunch.
Debutant Herchelle Gibbs, twice let off the hook by substitute fielder Sanjay Manjrekar, was finally beaten by a slower ball from Prasad and was out leg before wicket.
Gibbs' wicket fell when the score was 346. He hit 31, including five fours, off 112 balls.
Skipper Hansie Cronje lasted just 18 balls when he got an edge off fast bowler Javagal Srinath. Wicket-keeper Nayan Mongia took the catch.
Prasad bagged his second wicket when he trapped all-rounder Brian McMillan, facing his second delivery, leg before wicket.
Darryl Cullinan's was Prasad's third victim. His patient knock of 43 ended in another lbw, but he did not look happy with Sri Lankan umpire B.C. Cooray's decision.
All-rounder Lance Klusener was clean bowled by Prasad for 10.
South African wicket-keeper Dave Richardson on 25 and Pat Symcox on two were still at the crease.
